known.title: The results log decides C1 on the four panel cases only and leaves out the delta case that the plan puts in the deciding set
known.summary: Plan decision 3 (plan line 40) puts `code-111-r3-delta` in the new held-out code cases, and decision 5 (plan line 42) fixes the rule 'for each reviewer on its new held-out cases' before the runs. results.md:913 says 'Thus the code decision uses the panel cases', and the C1 decision at results.md:943 gives only the panel values (24.60 against 25.40 per 50 known). So the log changes the deciding set after the runs, and the decision that the plan fixed (all five code cases, pooled) is not reported, even if it also passes.

known.title: The plan-reviewer agent and skill call every Acceptance row that passes without the change a defect, also a regression guard or a gate
known.summary: plan-reviewer.md:31-33 says 'An Acceptance row that passes without the change is a defect of that row', and the skill constraint (plan-reviewer/SKILL.md:30-31) says 'An Acceptance row that cannot fail without the change is a load-bearing defect'. Both have no condition. The checklist (references/checklist.md:33 and 45-47) limits the rule to rows that check a Goal outcome and says that a regression guard or a gate is not a finding, and plan decision 1 (P1, plan line 36) asks for the same limit in 'the matching lines in the agent and the skill'. A gate row such as `bun scripts/ci.mjs` exits 0 passes before the steps, so a reviewer that follows the agent or skill text reports it and adds a repair round.

known.title: The reader check calls an unchanged reader a finding without evidence that it misreads the new form
known.summary: checklist.md:68-73 tells the plan reviewer to search for each reader of an old form and says 'A reader on a supported path that no step updates is a finding.' It asks for no evidence that the reader breaks. A reader that handles the new form, for example score.mjs, which lists arm folders generically, then becomes a finding when a plan adds arm names. The reviewer so asks for consumer edits that the plan does not need.

known.title: The skill says that a baseline panel prompt holds the lens text, which is false for the new B3 arm
known.summary: SKILL.md:110 says 'A panel prompt of a baseline agent holds the lens text'. The new `B3` arm runs the baseline agent with the candidate prompt, which only names the lens (prepare.mjs:149, 428-432, 458; SKILL.md:104). An operator who picks a baseline ref without lens references for `B3` expects the lens text in the prompt and does not get it. The text must limit this to `B1` and say that `B3` needs a baseline reviewer that loads its lens references.

known.title: The Codex wrappers give no location of the installed plugin, so a failed lookup falls back to the project-local reviewer that the diff can change
known.summary: Both wrappers and both templates say to load the reviewer from the installed plan-lifecycle plugin and to use the project-local `plugins/plan-lifecycle/agents/<role>.md` 'only when no installed plugin exists'. They name no path, variable, or input for the installed copy, so the reviewer cannot tell 'no installed plugin' from 'lookup failed'. It then loads the project-local copy, which the diff or plan under review can change, and nothing in its block shows this. The same text says that this copy 'must not set the review rules' (line 10), and plan decision 7 (plan line 44) wants that no diff can change the instructions of its own review. The wrapper must name the Codex plugin cache and refuse (return `blocked`) when the review input changes the reviewer files.

known.title: The plan contract still tells code reviewers to treat a recorded decision as settled, against the new code-reviewer precedence
known.summary: C1 ranks the plan contract above recorded decisions (code-reviewer/SKILL.md:31-37) and says that a decision 'does not settle the facts that it relies on, or an effect that breaks...' (lines 39-41, 71-78). The contract, Delegation line (plan-contract.md:637-639), still says without condition 'Code reviewers treat a recorded decision as settled.', next to the plan-reviewer sentence that adds 'report a false premise or a broken effect'. On a yolo plan, the higher-ranked contract tells the code reviewer to drop the false-fact and broken-effect findings that C1 adds. plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md asks to coordinate edits across the surfaces when a concept changes.

known.title: Two prepare.mjs comments still say that every baseline panel prompt describes the lens, which is false for B3
known.summary: The comment above PANEL_RULES (prepare.mjs:179-182) says 'A panel prompt of the baseline agent ... describes the lens in the dispatch', and the buildTail comment (lines 420-421) says 'A panel tail of another agent describes the lens'. `B3` is a baseline-agent panel arm without lens text, and buildTail now gets `spec.prompt ?? side` (line 458), a prompt shape and not the agent side, in its parameter `side`. A maintainer who trusts these comments misreads which arms describe the lens.

known.title: The judge rubric needs the quoted rule to apply and its effect to hold, but the plan says the rule or the effect
known.summary: Plan decision 2 (plan line 39) makes such a finding `valid` 'when its rule or effect holds', and results.md restates the 'or'. judge.md:33 says 'rate it `valid` when the rule that it quotes applies to the path and its effect holds'. A finding that shows that recorded behavior breaks the correctness of the code quotes no rule, so a judge that reads judge.md literally rates it `wrong`, and it counts against the wrong-per-run bound of decision 5.

known.title: The loop-policy test leaves out the new B3 arm, so no test shows that case and loop give B3 the C3 prompts
known.summary: `B3` gets `policy: 'panel-delta'` (prepare.mjs:149), so `case --arms B3 --loop` and `loop` accept it. But POLICY_ARMS (review-benchmark.test.mjs:4091) and the expected modes of the loop test (lines 4164-4167) leave out `B3`, and the new prompt test calls buildPromptFile with its default spec, while `case` takes the spec from armSpec. No test shows that `case` and `loop` write `B3` prompt files equal to the `C3` ones, which is the path that the dev and held-out runs use.

known.title: The round-policy table of the review loop lists only C3 and B1 under panel-delta and leaves out B3
known.summary: The Arms table (SKILL.md:92-96) and prepare.mjs:149 give the new `B3` arm the policy `panel-delta`, but the policy table of the Review loop (SKILL.md:234) lists only `C3` and `B1` for that policy. An operator who picks a `--loop` arm from this table does not find `B3`.

known.title: The code-reviewer agent's fallback rules leave out the base-text rule for a changed instruction file
known.summary: code-reviewer.md:14-15 says that the agent rules are enough for a `full` round when the skill cannot load. Its new step 4 (lines 41-44) applies the `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` files of the touched paths, but it leaves out the skill rule (code-reviewer/SKILL.md:56-60) to apply the text before the change when the diff changes an instruction file or the plan contract. In that fallback, a diff that weakens an instruction file is reviewed under the weakened text, which is the risk that the plan gives as a reason for C1.
